checks: Matched 5a3c8a5af6aaf266:4–5 §3. A nonconstant nonnegative affine function is positive on int(D). Take a disk at a fixed positive level inside an interior ball. Homothety from the zero x₀ scales the (d−1)-area of its level-s section by (s/s₀)^(d−1). The affine coarea factor is 1/‖c‖; the lower integral is divergent precisely for r≥d, logarithmic at equality. In d=1 the disk is one point and its zero-dimensional measure is one.

If h is identically zero, its extended integrand is infinite on D of positive volume. In the moving case a fixed interior point of D has positive support margin, so it belongs to D_j eventually. Coefficient convergence then gives the extended pointwise limit h^−r there. Fatou over the zero-extended nonnegative integrands gives divergence without requiring the limiting zero to lie in any D_j.

For the simplex, volume below t=∑x_i is t^d times the total volume, giving density d·t^(d−1) for uniform t. Monotone convergence gives mean d/(d−r) for 0<r<d. Multiplying h_δ by that moving mean to the 1/r power gives mean-one inverse power exactly, with finite nonzero limiting scale and an affine function vanishing at the vertex.

overlap.comparison: Its proof explicitly credits the same fixed-fiber cone argument at p=d+1 for mixed face minimization. The frozen statement adds the critical exponent d, arbitrary r≥d, moving-body Fatou, and the sharp subcritical family.

Shows fixed-body blow-up for admissible denominators approaching the boundary at exponent d+1, using a shrinking annulus of cone parameters. It does not cover the full exponent range, the joint moving-body setting or sharpness.

readability: The displayed log divergence refers to the cone lower bound. Some geometries can have a stronger divergence, consistent with the statement.
